findings.text: blocking: evidence: the mean nDCG@10 comparison that selects and justifies the deployed variant is invalid. docs_ties_eval.py:58-64 copies the prototype's ndcg_at_10, whose ideal set (idcg) is sorted over the SAME ordered list it scores, so when a variant changes which chunks are in the 30-list the denominator changes with it. The reserve20/reserve20_cos variants swap every rank 10-29 for vector leaders while pinning the top 10, so the displayed top 10 for every question is bit-identical to the baseline (verified across all 18: baseline_top30[:10] == reserve20_top30[:10]) and DCG@10 is therefore identical - measured q06 DCG@10 1.9200 in both arms, q09 1.8740 both, q15 1.5000 both - while the reported ndcg rises only because relevant documents leave the 30-window and shrink IDCG (q06 IDCG 4.5436->2.1309 as nrel in the window falls 10->3; q09 4.5436->2.5616 as 16->4; q15 2.9485->2.1309 as 5->3). The headline gain 0.2763->0.3672 measures the ideal pool shrinking, not a ranking gain; on the two docs questions where it matters the deployed change still leaves Q14 and Q18 nDCG@10 at 0.0000 (their answers land at ranks 15 and 13, outside the k=10 the metric reads). The real, defensible effect the change delivers is the answers entering the k=30 window, which the fragment also states; the nDCG@10 figure the fragment leads with does not support the deployed variant.

blocking: evidence: the eval's own reimplemented baseline does not reproduce the stored prototype order on the docs questions it is meant to measure. variant_metrics.json reproduction shows overlap_top30 of 11/30 (q13), 14/30 (q18), 15/30 (q14), 16/30 (q15), 17/30 (q17), 25/30 (q16) for the docs questions, against 29-30/30 for every code question. docs_ties_eval.py:97-117 calls the tool's own stage functions but re-derives the merge in merge_score() (docs_ties_eval.py:67-85), and on the docs path - which is exactly the path the change targets and where the 1.0 tie mass lives - that reimplementation diverges from the tool on up to 19 of 30 positions. Every nDCG, answer-rank and variant number is computed on that non-reproducing order, so the measurement is not shown to describe the tool it claims to measure. The 18-question mean is also computed with the reserve applied to the 13 code questions although the deployed change is _search_docs only, mixing a change that is not deployed into the headline mean.

follow-on: durability: the load-bearing half of the change is untested. The added test test_cosine_breaks_saturated_score_ties uses n=8 chunks at k=30, so _reserve_vector_leaders never reserves a slot (its top-10 path alone runs) - the test exercises only the (score, cosine) sort key. _reserve_vector_leaders (search_tools.py:691-711), which is what actually lifts Q14/Q18 into the window and what removes the baseline's ranks 10-29, has no test: nothing asserts that the top 10 is preserved, that a vector leader outside the top 10 is promoted to rank 10, or that no chunk is duplicated. The cosine tie-break the test does cover is, by the node's own fragment (line 60), the part that 'cannot lift the answers'. A mutation that drops the reserve entirely would keep the suite green.

follow-on: goal: _reserve_vector_leaders replaces every rank 10-29 of the hybrid order with the facility's vector leaders, dropping hybrid-ranked chunks that the keyword term promoted. On docs questions this trades relevant documents out of the window (q15 nrel in the 30-list 5->3) against the answers it brings in (q14 0->1, q18 0->3). The plan's selection rule ('keeps Q16 and lifts the most answers into the top 30') ties at two answers for reserve20_cos, reserve20 and noclamp_reserve, and the node deployed reserve20_cos (mean 0.3672) over noclamp_reserve (mean 0.4081), which keeps Q16 at 0.9675 and lifts the same two answers; the node's stated reason (the clamp keeps the displayed score range) is a reasonable display argument but is not the measured criterion. This is a judgement call to surface, not a defect to fix here.

follow-on: fit: the fragment's Files list cites reports/imas-codex/docs-score-ties/new_labels.json, which does not exist - the report directory holds base_arm.log, debug_q14.py, docs_ties_eval.py, eval.log, gate.log, negative_control.log, run_eval.py, run_negative_control.py and variant_metrics.json only; the new labels are embedded under the new_labels key of variant_metrics.json (top-level key 'new_labels'), as docs_ties_eval.py:240 writes them. A later reader following the cited path finds nothing.

follow_ons: the reviewed manifest should carry its baseline_suite and after_suite fields so the added-failure annotation is measured at read time rather than by hand; the docs_ties_eval.py ndcg_at_10 copies the prototype's pool-relative ideal and needs a fixed relevance pool before it can compare variants that change the candidate set; the eval's docs-path merge should be replaced by a call to _search_docs so the numbers describe the tool; _reserve_vector_leaders needs a test.

justifications.durability: durability 12: a real test with a real negative control exists for the deterministic tie-break, but the reserve behaviour that produces the claimed effect is untested and could regress silently.
justifications.evidence: evidence 9: raw per-query output, logs, a valid negative control and a base arm are recorded, but the headline metric is invalid as a cross-variant comparison, the eval does not reproduce the tool on the docs path (11-25/30), and the 18-question mean mixes in a non-deployed change.
justifications.fit: fit 17: the change follows §9's idiom, names the helper and constants by mechanism, carries no plan or ticket label, and the fragment follows its sibling's structure; one cited file does not exist.
justifications.goal_fidelity: goal_fidelity 15: the literal goal and the test are delivered, but the variant selection the plan prescribes is justified by a metric that does not measure ranking, and the deployed variant is not the one the (broken) metric would pick.
justifications.reuse: reuse 15: the eval calls the tool's own stage functions, but copies the prototype's ndcg_at_10 into a comparison it does not hold for and reimplements the merge in merge_score rather than exercising _search_docs.
justifications.scope_discipline: scope_discipline 19: only _search_docs is changed, _search_code is untouched as required, no graph write, no discover run, and every landed path is inside the declared set.
